A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ξ-VI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching reordered theory sections and renamed supplementary sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original Laplace linear-regression simulations and eight-schools posterior comparisons in Section 3 and the supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds a replicated study of Monte Carlo support size in Appendix F, Table 1.

M1.justification: The expressivity-regularized objective, EOT coupling, Algorithms 1–3, and grouped regression implementation are retained. Added discussion of generalized posteriors and minibatching does not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Gaussian example, the same simulated regression with 100 observations and 12 features, and the eight-schools dataset. Varying support size in v4 changes settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain EP and MFVI for regression, and MFVI, NFVI, full-rank ADVI, and SVGD for eight schools, with MCMC posterior references. MFVI also already appears in v3's Figure 6.

E3.justification: Figures 2(b) and 5(b) replace iteration counts at Sinkhorn tolerance 10^-4 with seconds at 10^-5. Figure 6 changes the reported covariance-error metric from spectral to Frobenius norm. The added study varies N from 5 to 35 at λ=10.

E4.justification: Appendix F, Table 1 adds a support-size sensitivity analysis, examining how N affects posterior mean error, covariance error, Wasserstein distance, and runtime. This supplies evidence for the previously used N=20 choice.

E5.justification: The new Table 1 reports medians and interquantile ranges across 20 experimental replicates, although the quantile levels are unspecified. This supplements the existing posterior credible intervals and MCMC reporting; it does not establish increased replication of retained experiments.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports, for example, median W2 error/runtime of 0.196/3.458 seconds at N=20 and 0.178/32.286 seconds at N=35. Runtime and covariance-error curves are replaced under revised settings or metrics. The main accuracy panels and school-pair interval values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 explicitly requires an interior true parameter and a shrinking LAN scaling matrix, and adds a short KL comparison derivation in Section 3.1. It removes the earlier high-dimensional BvM-based covariance simplification and the definition of B′_diag despite retaining its use. The main theorems and appendix proofs otherwise largely survive renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: entropic relaxation of mean-field VI, Sinkhorn-based computation, frequentist guarantees, statistical-computational tradeoffs, and empirical inferential benefits.

C2.justification: v4 expands discussion of generalized-loss posteriors, explains the compact-domain scope of the high-dimensional results, and discusses extensions to unbounded domains under log-concavity. It also interprets the new support-size results and more explicitly identifies the averaging bottleneck motivating minibatching.

D1.justification: v4 adds configurations and elapsed-time information for the support-size study, alongside explicit discussion of full-tensor memory and averaging costs. The existing 20-point discretization, coefficient grouping, and MCMC settings were already documented in v3.

R1.justification: New citations broaden the existing discussion of generalized and tempered posteriors, support-size sensitivity, and high-dimensional theory, including Bissiri et al., Frazier et al., and Zhong et al. Panov–Spokoiny and Katsevich are removed with the covariance simplification. Publication updates to retained references do not change positioning.

P1.justification: v4 reverses the two theory subsections, consolidates assumptions, revises explanatory and computational prose, and labels the supplementary analyses Appendices F and G. Journal front matter and acknowledgments are updated. The overall narrative and most exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 adds the support-size table, redraws Figure 6 with a new axis label and styling, and revises the runtime panels and captions. Figures and algorithms are repositioned or reformatted, while the overall single-column layout and most graphical content are retained.

improvement.justification: The replicated support-size study provides useful evidence for the existing N=20 choice, elapsed-time plots make computational costs more practical to assess, and clearer theory-scope explanations aid interpretation. These limited gains outweigh the small regression from removing the B′_diag definition. The changed metrics and tolerances do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
